item.title: Nonproduct Minimal Submanifolds with Cylindrical Tangent Cones
item.description: arXiv:2610.20862v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article constructs, via perturbation methods, infinite-dimensional families of non-product minimal submanifolds which have singular sets locally modeled on cylindrical tangent cones. This answers a question raised by Leon Simon in the 1980s, and generalizes work Caffarelli-Hardt-Simon, who treated the case of isolated singularities. This setting requires substantially more work, however, since the natural obstruction space for the problem is infinite dimensional and the map which is meant to compensate for this obstruction using deformations of the singular set exhibits a loss of regularity. This necessitates working in the category of tame Frechet spaces and using the Nash-Moser Implicit Function Theorem.
item.dc:creator: Rafe Mazzeo, Gregory J. Parker

item.title: Quantitative Volume Estimate on Singular Sets of One-phase Free Boundary Problems in Ricci Limit Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.20986v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study limit solutions of the one-phase free boundary problem on noncollapsed Ricci limit spaces. We introduce a quantitative stratification $\mathcal{S}^k_{\varepsilon,r}$ of the singular set of the free boundary that simultaneously captures the approximate splitting of the ambient space and the approximate homogeneity and translational invariance of the solution. We also introduce a new truncated parabolic Weiss quantity that provides quantitative homogeneity via pinching across scales. Although this quantity may not be uniformly bounded across all small scales, it effectively shows that, among the first $j$ scales in a fixed decreasing geometric progression, at most $C\sqrt{j}$ scales fail to exhibit quantitative homogeneity. Such slow growth in $j$ enables us to adapt the covering argument of Cheeger and Naber [arXiv:1103.1819] to show, for every $\eta>0$, a $Cr^{n-k-\eta}$ upper bound for the volume of the $r$-tubular neighborhood of the $k$-th quantitative singular stratum, $\mathcal{S}^k_{\varepsilon,r}$. The same tubular-neighborhood estimate holds for the effective stratum $\mathcal S_\varepsilon^k$, and in particular we get the Minkowski dimension bound $\dim_{\mathcal M} \mathcal S_\varepsilon^k \le k$, from which the previously known sharp bound $\dim_{\mathcal H} \mathrm{Sing} \le n-3$ in Chan, Zhang, and Zhu [arXiv:2112.06962] follows. As another corollary, we prove that the free boundary admits a H\"older manifold structure away from a set of Minkowski dimension at most $n-3$.
item.dc:creator: Alejandro Bellati, Kai-Hsiang Wang

item.title: Infinitely many closed geodesic images on simply connected compact rank-one symmetric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.21054v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every smooth Riemannian metric on the underlying smooth manifold of a simply connected compact rank-one symmetric space, namely $S^n$ $(n\ge2)$, $\CP^m$ $(m\ge1)$, $\HP^m$ $(m\ge1)$, or $\OP^2$ admits infinitely many geometrically distinct prime closed geodesics. Here a prime closed geodesic is a nonconstant closed geodesic which is not an iterate of a shorter one, and geometric distinctness means that the images in the manifold are pairwise different. Thus iterating a geodesic, changing its starting point, or reversing its orientation does not count as a new geodesic. No nondegeneracy assumption on the metric is imposed. These manifolds have bounded loop-space Betti numbers, so the usual homological growth criterion does not yield this conclusion. We use the length filtration together with rotation and reversal of loops. A controlled cut construction gives a uniform filling estimate in the based loop space, with a fixed increase in length independent of degree, which we transfer to free loops. We then calculate global equivariant classes associated with odd and even iterates. Assuming finitely many prime geodesic images forces incompatible requirements at a class's first critical level. The proof treats spheres and projective spaces within a common framework and does not assume a sphere infinitude theorem.
item.dc:creator: Zhiqi Chen, Shaoqiang Deng, Hui Zhang

item.title: Complete steady gradient Yamabe solitons
item.description: arXiv:2610.21078v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we show that nontrivial complete steady gradient Yamabe solitons are either rotationally symmetric manifolds or scalar-flat manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Shun Maeta

item.title: Understanding entropy using Aubin--Yau deformations
item.description: arXiv:2610.21198v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we investigate three types of entropy that frequently appear in the research of K\"ahler geometry: the classical K\"ahler entropy, the radial entropy and the non-Archimedean entropy. We give a unifying interpretation for these entropies by showing that they can all be expressed as the derivative of the Monge--Amp\`ere energy along certain Aubin--Yau type deformations. Such considerations also lead to a novel algebraic criterion for the existence of constant scalar curvature K\"ahler metrics.
item.dc:creator: Tam\'as Darvas, Kewei Zhang

item.title: Asymptotics of the Moduli Spaces of Parabolic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb C)$-Higgs Bundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.21303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the large-scale geometry of the moduli spaces of stable strongly parabolic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\C)$-Higgs bundles on the three-punctured sphere for a family of parabolic weights. We glue the local Toda model metric to a decoupled metric obtained from the spectral line bundle, and perturb the resulting approximate metrics to harmonic metrics adapted to the parabolic structure. We also prove that Hitchin's $L^2$ metric approaches the semi-flat metric exponentially. The metric comparison and the spectral period calculation show that each moduli space is a complete ALG gravitational instanton of type $E_6$. The asymptotic estimates are uniform on compact subintervals of the weight chamber.
item.dc:creator: Shiyu Cao

item.title: Finite Time Noncollapsing K\"ahler-Ricci Flow: Gaussian Type Heat Kernel, Gromov-Hausdorff Limits
item.description: arXiv:2610.21824v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study heat kernel estimates along the K\"ahler-Ricci flow with finite time noncollapsing singularities over a compact K\"ahler manifold. The starting point is the type-II scalar-curvature estimate, which gives the natural parabolic scale $r\lesssim T-t$ near the singular time. By combining the distance distortion and space-time cut-off estimates of Bamler--Zhang with entropy, mean-value inequality, and conjugate heat-kernel estimates, we obtain two-sided Gaussian bounds and gradient bounds that are uniform on this scale. Under the global type-I scalar-curvature estimate, the same estimates hold on every scale. We then use these estimates and the monotonicity of the $W_1$-distance between conjugate heat flows to construct a canonical singular-time pseudo-distance. The distances $d_t$ (induced by $\omega(t)$) converge uniformly to this pseudo-distance. Its metric quotient is the unique Gromov--Hausdorff limit. Finally, we apply Bamler's theory and the recent work of Hallgren--Zhang to obtain the following. Every fixed-base-point type-I blow-up admits a subsequential metric-flow limit whose time slices are singular shrinking K\"ahler--Ricci soliton spaces with normal complex-analytic and log-terminal structure, unique tangent cones, and a polarized Fano fibration. For moving base points, the limiting metric flow, equipped with its limiting conjugate heat flow, is a metric soliton precisely under an entropy-pinching condition.
item.dc:creator: Lei Zhang, Zhenlei Zhang

item.title: Cohomogeneity one Hermann actions and backward mean curvature flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.21884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Principal orbits of cohomogeneity one Hermann actions form a natural class of equifocal hypersurfaces in symmetric spaces of compact type. Based on Kollross's classification of cohomogeneity one actions on irreducible symmetric spaces of compact type, we obtain the time evolution of the squared norm of the shape operator and the mean curvature along the long-time solution of the backward mean curvature flows starting from their principal orbits. These results explicitly describe the authors' previous generalization of the results of Liu-Terng on backward mean curvature flows of isoparametric hypersurfaces to this class of equifocal hypersurfaces.
item.dc:creator: Kurando Baba, Naoyuki Koike

item.title: Local Convexity and Planarity Estimates for Mean Curvature Flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.21903v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish local convexity and cylindrical pinching estimates for hypersurface mean curvature flow under an intermediate convexity condition and integral bounds on the mean curvature. These estimates hold after a positive waiting time and do not require pointwise upper bounds for the mean curvature on the parabolic boundary. In arbitrary codimension, we also establish local planarity estimates for properly defined flows satisfying a uniform $c_n$-pinching condition, without assuming bounded curvature. As applications, the hypersurface estimates yield convexity and cylindrical pinching for complete, spacetime-proper ancient hypersurface flows with uniform Euclidean area growth, without any bounded-curvature assumption. The planarity estimates imply that every complete, connected, spacetime-proper ancient flow satisfying the uniform $c_n$-pinching condition is either a static affine $n$-plane or lies in a fixed affine $(n+1)$-plane for all time.
item.dc:creator: Liang Cheng

item.title: Explicit Ricci-flat metrics on a special Schoen threefold
item.description: arXiv:2610.21932v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an explicit convergent representation of the Ricci-flat K\"ahler metric in a one-parameter family of classes on a fixed special Schoen threefold. The threefold resolves a shifted square-torus quotient with sixteen disjoint elliptic singular curves. Radial Eguchi--Hanson product metrics and fixed flat collars define a positive background with an exact $a^4$ volume defect. Spherical harmonics, tangential Fourier modes, Frobenius recurrences, radial ordered integrals, and the flat quotient heat kernel specify the inverse of the background scalar linearized operator. A boundary transmission series has contraction factor $1/15$. Independent weighted zeroth-order and six-dimensional Schauder estimates give the inverse bound needed for the quadratic and cubic Monge--Amp\`ere terms. The resulting source-degree recursion converges for $0<a\le2^{-2260}$, with explicit coefficient, potential-tail, and relative metric-tail bounds. The representation uses specified kernels, prescribed integrals, and convergent series; its parameter interval is a sufficient quantitative bound on this fixed model.
item.dc:creator: Jixiang Fu, Jiuhe Liu, Yunyang Xiao, Shing-Tung Yau

item.title: Gromov-Hausdorff Convergence of Constant Scalar Curvature K\"ahler Metrics near the Canonical Class
item.description: arXiv:2610.21934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X$ be a compact K\"ahler manifold with semi-ample canonical bundle. For any K\"ahler class $[\omega]$, Jian--Shi--Song proved that there exists a unique cscK metric in the class $2\pi c_1(K_X)+\varepsilon[\omega]$ when $\varepsilon \in (0,\varepsilon_0]$, using the properness criterion of Chen--Cheng. We prove that the cscK metrics in $2\pi c_1(K_X)+\varepsilon[\omega]$ converge, as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, in the Gromov--Hausdorff topology to the metric completion of the twisted K\"ahler-Einstein metric on the canonical model of $X$ as conjectured by Jian--Shi--Song. Based on the technique developed in this paper, we can also give a new proof the theorem of Lee--Tosatti--Zhang on the Gromov-Hausdorff convergence of the normalized K\"ahler--Ricci flow on $X$.
item.dc:creator: Frederick Tsz-Ho Fong, Junbang Liu

item.title: Mod 3 Congruence Families for twisted signatures of string manifolds in dimensions up to twenty-eight
item.description: arXiv:2610.21959v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the paper, we establish congruences for twisted Dirac indices and signatures on closed string manifolds by specializing the two-parameter modular forms of Liu and Wang to the tangent bundle. Fourier coefficient comparisons yield uniform congruences modulo $3$ in dimensions $4k$, $1\leq k\leq7$. Suitable parameter choices give explicit formulas involving only genuine twisting bundles in dimensions $8,12,16,20,24,$ and $28$, and recover the comparisons of Chen and Han in dimension $24$. The level-one Witten genus further strengthens selected Dirac congruences to moduli $729,27,27,$ and $9$ in dimensions $16,20,24,$ and $28$, respectively. The proofs use Fourier expansions in reduced $K$-theory and integer identities obtained by clearing powers of two from the denominators before reduction modulo $3$. We also construct non-string spin counterexamples in each of the six listed dimensions and identify the additional coefficient that obstructs extending the uniform argument to dimension $32$ without further information.
item.dc:creator: Tong Wu, Yong Wang

item.title: The derived category of a generalized complex torus
item.description: arXiv:2610.21960v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For any translation invariant generalized complex structure J on a torus we construct the derived category D(J) generalizing the derived category of coherent sheaves on a complex torus and the affine/convergent Fukaya category of a symplectic torus. The category is defined in terms of a non-commutative curved deformation of the Dolbeault algebra of a complex torus. We show that this category is independent of the chosen deformation path, which we prove using non-commutative Fourier-Mukai duality. We also prove that the action of O(2n,2n; Z) on the space of generalized complex structures leaves the category D(J) invariant. In particular, T-duality acts trivially on D(J). We construct concrete objects associated to affine Lagrangians in the derived category associated to a symplectic torus and show that their spaces of morphisms are given by Floer cohomology. We show that our construction is consistent with the homological mirror symmetry conjecture (including its non-commutative version).
item.dc:creator: Patrick Antweiler, Vicente Cort\'es, Julian Holstein, Markus R\"oser, Aldo Witte

item.title: Singular Yamabe metrics on complements of closed sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.21963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $n\geq3$ and let $\Lambda\subset \mathbb S^n$ be closed, contain at least two points, and satisfy $\dim_{\mathrm H}\Lambda<(n-2)/2$. We prove that there exists a complete metric of scalar curvature $n(n-1)$ on $\mathbb S ^n\setminus\Lambda$, conformal to the round metric.
item.dc:creator: Weiyang Li, Heng Zhang

item.title: Schwarz $\mathrm{P}$ and Schwarz $\mathrm{D}$ as free-boundary minimal disks in a tetragonal disphenoid: exact areas
item.description: arXiv:2610.22013v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $T$ be the tetragonal disphenoid whose four congruent faces are isosceles triangles with sides $2,\sqrt3,\sqrt3$, so that the dihedral angles are $\pi/2$ along one opposite pair of edges and $\pi/3$ along the remaining four. By Smyth's theorem $T$ contains three embedded minimal disks meeting $\partial T$ orthogonally; the symmetry group $D_{2d}$ of $T$ fixes one and interchanges the other two. We identify all three completely. The distinguished disk is a patch of $\textbf{Schwarz's $\mathrm{P}$ surface}$ and the congruent pair are patches of $\textbf{Schwarz's $\mathrm{D}$ surface}$, with exact areas \[ \operatorname{Area}(\Sigma^{*}_{A}) = \frac{K\!\left(\tfrac14\right)} {K\!\left(\tfrac34\right)} = 0.781700961348056\ldots, \] \[ \operatorname{Area}(\Sigma^{*}_{B}) = \frac{K\!\left(\tfrac34\right)} {2\,K\!\left(\tfrac14\right)} = 0.639630785585503\ldots \] in the normalization $\operatorname{Vol}(T)=2/3$, inradius $r_T=\sqrt2/4$. In particular $2\,\operatorname{Area}(\Sigma^{*}_{A})\operatorname{Area}(\Sigma^{*}_{B})=1$, which we show is the Bonnet relation for the adjoint pair $(\mathrm{D},\mathrm{P})$. The proof is a reversal of the usual strategy: rather than uniformizing the Gauss map, we identify Smyth's three Plateau contours as the $\textit{tetrahedral four edges}$ and the $\textit{octahedral four edges}$ --- classically solved by $\mathrm{D}$ and $\mathrm{P}$ respectively --- and then conjugate. Both areas agree with Surface Evolver computations of Ken Brakke to all $15$ reported digits. We also show that all twelve corners of the three disks are midpoints of edges of $T$, each of the six midpoints being used twice, and that $T$ is precisely the alcove of the affine Weyl group $\widetilde{A}_{3}$, confirming a remark of Gandy, Cvijovi\'c, et al. (1999).
item.dc:creator: Steven Finch

item.title: The Hopf conjecture with $T^3$-symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2610.22173v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that any closed even-dimensional manifold with positive sectional curvature admitting an isometric action by a 3-torus has positive Euler characteristic. We also prove the result for orbifolds.
item.dc:creator: Jan Nienhaus, Dennis Wulle

item.title: Observing minimal submanifolds with isolated singularities on open sets of metrics
item.description: arXiv:2610.22229v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a perturbative theory for minimal submanifolds with only (strongly) isolated singularities, with respect to varying background Riemannian metrics. As an application, we obtain a general "sporadic persistence" criterion, thus naturally complementing the non-persistence theorem by the authors. In particular, such a criterion is satisfied by the spherical suspension in $\mathbb{S}^{3m+2}$ of the Veronese embedding of $\mathbb{K}\mathbb{P}^2$ for $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C},\mathbb{H},\mathbb{O}$ (the normed division algebras) in the round spheres of dimension $3m+1=4,7,13,25$ respectively, thereby providing families of continuously varying $(2m+1)$-dimensional stationary varifolds with isolated singularities that are observable on an open set of metrics. By our previous results, these phenomena cannot possibly occur in the codimension one scenario.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Carlotto, Yangyang Li, Zhihan Wang

item.title: Extending Donaldson's HyperK\"ahler Structure via Minimal Surfaces into $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C})$
item.description: arXiv:2610.22288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a deformation space for minimal immersions into $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C})$ with its holomorphic Killing form, and define an explicit, mapping class group invariant, complex hyperK\"ahler structure on such deformation space. Such complex hyperK\"ahler structure restricts to: Donaldson's hyperK\"ahler structure on a totally real copy of almost-Fuchsian space, Mazzoli-Seppi-Tamburelli's para-hyperK\"ahler structure on a totally real copy of maximally globally hyperbolic $\mathbb{A}\mathrm{d}\mathbb{S}^3$ manifolds, and Loustau-Sanders' complex bi-K\"ahler structure on a holomorphic copy of quasi-Fuchsian space. Moreover, all these loci are totally geodesic. We discuss other geometric aspects of this space, such as the Hamiltonian property of a natural $\mathbb{C}^*$-action, involving the Goldman symplectic form and a complex-valued area functional.
item.dc:creator: Christian El Emam, Filippo Mazzoli, Nicholas Rungi, Andrea Seppi, Andrea Tamburelli

item.title: Stratification of opers with apparent singularities and isomonodromic bubbling
item.description: arXiv:2610.22326v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On a compact Riemann surface of genus $g \geq 2$, we study Simpson's stratification of the de Rham moduli space of rank-2 flat connections. Upon representing flat $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$-connections by branched projective structures, or equivalently by opers with apparent singularities, the stratum containing a flat connection is determined by the minimal number of apparent singularities needed to represent it. We construct explicit holomorphic families in which two simple apparent singularities collide and disappear, so that the family crosses into a smaller stratum; this realizes Simpson's closure relation between strata near generic points. The analogous families of Higgs bundles are described by Baker--Akhiezer divisors on the spectral curve in which two points converge to a pair of points exchanged by the spectral involution. We show that, before the collision, the two apparent singularities are joined by twin paths bounding a bubble, so that these families arise from the isomonodromic bubbling surgery discussed by Calsamiglia, Deroin and Francaviglia.
item.dc:creator: Duong Dinh, Troy Figiel, Joerg Teschner

item.title: Polynomial Maximal Surfaces in H^{2,2} and Spherical Polygons
item.description: arXiv:2610.22329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the moduli space of complete maximal surfaces in pseudo-hyperbolic space $\mathbf{H}^{2,2}$ with polygonal asymptotic boundary a lightlike $(n+4)$-gon in the Einstein universe $\mathbf{Ein}^{1,2}$, up to the action of $\mathsf{SO}_0(2,3)$. Importantly, this space $M_{n+4}(\mathbf{H}^{2,2})$ is disconnected for $n\geq 2$. We introduce a \emph{turning invariant} $\Theta$ that classifies the components in terms of the geometry of the boundary polygons in the Einstein universe $\mathbf{Ein}^{1,2}$, which is related to \emph{spherical polygons} in $\mathbb{S}^2$. We provide a geometric parametrization of the moduli space $M_{n+4}(\mathbf{H}^{2,2})$ via holomorphic data, namely a pair of polynomials $\alpha$, $\beta$. These polynomials appear in relation to certain components of the complexified second fundamental form of the corresponding surface. We then relate the holomorphic data $\alpha,\beta$ with the turning invariant $\Theta$. This leads to characterizations of the \emph{Hitchin component} of polygonal maximal surfaces studied by Tamburelli-Wolf.
item.dc:creator: Parker Evans, Alex Moriani

item.title: The \textsc{ABC}-equation revisited: missed integrable cases. Part I: classification and (quasi) integrable structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.20672v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the \textsc{ABC}-equation $Au_xu_{yt} + Bu_yu_{xt} + Cu_tu_{xy} = 0$, $A$, $B$, $C\in\mathbb{R}$, which was proved to be integrable in the case $A + B + C = 0$ (the Veronese web equation). Our study reveals ten more cases that admit integrable structures that, to the best of our knowledge, where not known before. The techniques is based essentially on the theory of the tangent and cotangent coverings.
item.dc:creator: I. S. Krasil'shchik

item.title: $p$-Laplace Serrin problem on planar annuli
item.description: arXiv:2610.20861v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a rigidity result for the problem $\Delta_p u=-2$ defined on a ring-shaped domain in $\mathbb{R}^2$, when homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions are imposed and $p\in(1,2)$. This problem admits a natural physical interpretation, as it describes the steady laminar flow of a generalised Newtonian fluid exhibiting shear-thinning behaviour. Our symmetry result is obtained assuming that the set of maximum points, denoted by $\Sigma$, is a smooth closed curve, and there are no other critical points outside it; moreover, an appropriate asymptotic expansion of the solution near $\Sigma$ is required. Although our approach is inspired by the comparison strategy of [arXiv:2505.04458], the main ingredients used there are intrinsically linear and have no direct counterparts for the $p$-Laplacian. This requires the introduction of new ideas and techniques.
item.dc:creator: Virginia Agostiniani, Chiara Bernardini

item.title: Symplectic groupoid multiplication and Poisson integrators
item.description: arXiv:2610.20911v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the role of local symplectic groupoid multiplication in the construction of approximation methods for Hamiltonian flows on the underlying Poisson manifold. We show it can be used to construct a novel multiplicative type of approximating sequences for the relevant Lagrangian bisection. We describe the corresponding theoretical results, their practical implementation into approximation methods on coordinate charts via generating functions, and illustrative examples.
item.dc:creator: Alejandro Cabrera, David Iglesias Ponte, Juan Carlos Marrero

item.title: Formation of Trapped Surfaces for the Einstein-Euler System
item.description: arXiv:2610.21124v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the formation of trapped surfaces for the Einstein--Euler system in 3+1 dimensions beyond spherical symmetry. We consider smooth characteristic initial data in a short-pulse regime with rapid fluid injection. Starting from initial data containing no trapped surfaces, we obtain two sufficient criteria for trapped surface formation, corresponding to the shear and fluid contributions, respectively. In particular, for the fluid-driven criterion, we impose no positive lower bound on the shear flux. To handle the multiple propagation speeds associated with gravitational waves, sound waves, and fluid transport, our analysis combines three ingredients: a coercive fluid energy current whose null fluxes reflect the unequal velocity components, curvature renormalizations adapted to the matter terms, and weighted geometric estimates controlling derivatives in all spacetime directions. To ensure that fluid injection alone can lead to trapped surface formation, we use particle-number conservation in a designed spacetime region to control the focusing process and obtain the desired sphere-integrated fluxes.
item.dc:creator: Xinliang An, Sifan Yu

item.title: Fixed-spinor radial solutions of a perturbed Euclidean spinorial Yamabe equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.21471v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the perturbed Euclidean spinorial Yamabe equation \[ D_{g_{\mathbb R^n}}\psi = \frac n2\bigl(1+\varepsilon K(x)\bigr) |\psi|^{2^*-2}\psi \qquad\text{on }\mathbb R^n,\quad n\ge2, \]where $2^*:=2n/(n-1)$, $\varepsilon>0$ is a small parameter and $K$ is a prescribed radial function. We establish a finite-dimensional reduction within a radial spinor space determined by a fixed unit spinor, reducing the problem to the analysis of a function of the dilation parameter. Under suitable assumptions on $K$, we obtain explicit existence criteria for solutions with this prescribed spinorial structure, together with a multiplicity criterion yielding solutions associated with distinct scales. These criteria are expressed in terms of the behavior of $K$ at the origin and weighted integral quantities.
item.dc:creator: Ting Li, Zhongwei Tang, Yuhang Zhang

item.title: Generic Mean Curvature Flow With Rough Weights
item.description: arXiv:2610.21545v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the generic existence of mean curvature flows in spaces with rough weights. Our weak solutions are both unit-density Brakke flows and distributional solutions. Such a generic statement is optimal in the sense that we consider weights that are too rough to have well-defined traces on every hypersurface.
item.dc:creator: Fabius Kr\"amer, Tim Laux, Keisuke Takasao

item.title: Causal Sobolev spaces and gradient flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.21775v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a relaxation-based approach to Sobolev functions and Cheeger energies on metric spacetimes, in analogy with the construction used in positive signature. For an exponent $p<0$, we introduce a pre-$p$-Cheeger energy built from a local steepness constant on causal functions, and define the $p$-Cheeger energy as its relaxation in $L^0$; this yields, by construction, a convex and lower semicontinuous functional together with an associated maximal relaxed subslope. We establish natural calculus rules for the resulting Sobolev class. We then define the $p$-heat flow as the gradient flow of the $p$-Cheeger energy in $L^2$ and its generator, the $p$-d'Alembertian. Combining a Kuwada-type lemma with entropy growth estimates along the flow, we show that our notion of Sobolev class and relaxed subslope coincides with the Sobolev class and weak subslope introduced by Beran et al.
item.dc:creator: Mathias Braun, Nicola Gigli, Robert McCann, Simone Vincini

item.title: Scalar curvature, volume, and Weil-Petersson translation length
item.description: arXiv:2610.21885v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct metrics on pseudoAnosov mapping tori that make every fiber an intrinsically hyperbolic stable minimal surface, and which have scalar curvature identically -6. Using this, we give a new proof (with improved constant) of an inequality bounding the hyperbolic volume of a pseudoAnosov mapping torus by the Weil-Petersson translation length (and consequently, the entropy) of its monodromy.
item.dc:creator: Cameron Gates Rudd

item.title: On the exact quantization of BCOV Theory on Calabi-Yau Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.21927v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We announce the solution of constructing perturbative quantum BCOV invariants on arbitrary Calabi-Yau manifolds. In this note, we outline the construction and present an explicit solution. The quantization includes all descendant fields and all loop orders, and expresses the quantum BCOV interaction by an explicit integration over the moduli space of marked Riemann surfaces. This canonical solution provides a mathematical construction of all higher genus BCOV invariants on compact Calabi-Yau manifolds, which are conjecturally equivalent to all higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants on the mirror.
item.dc:creator: Si Li, Minghao Wang

item.title: Counterexamples to the ordinary Fried conjecture near hyperbolic metrics
item.description: arXiv:2610.22281v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give an LLM-assisted construction of counterexamples to the ordinary Fried conjecture, with real analytic metrics arbitrarily close to a hyperbolic metric in dimension three. For acyclic unitary line characters tending to the trivial character, the modulus of the Ruelle zeta function at zero divided by analytic torsion squared tends to zero.
item.dc:creator: Simon Becker, Benjamin Lawton

item.title: Equivariant analytic torsion for proper actions
item.description: arXiv:2205.04117v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct an equivariant version of Ray-Singer analytic torsion for proper, isometric actions by locally compact groups on Riemannian manifolds, with compact quotients. We obtain results on convergence, metric independence, vanishing for even-dimensional manifolds, a product formula, and a decomposition of classical Ray-Singer analytic torsion as a sum over conjugacy classes of equivariant torsion on universal covers. We do explicit computations for the circle and the line acting on themselves, and for regular elliptic elements of $\operatorname{SO}_0(3,1)$ acting on $3$-dimensional hyperbolic space. Our constructions and results generalise several earlier constructions of equivariant analytic torsion and their properties, most of which apply to finite or compact groups, or to fundamental groups of compact manifolds acting on their universal covers. These earlier versions of equivariant analytic torsion were associated to finite or compact conjugacy classes; we allow noncompact conjugacy classes, under suitable growth conditions.
item.dc:creator: Peter Hochs, Hemanth Saratchandran

item.title: Contact Blow-up Analysis of the Legendrian Mean Curvature Flow and a Smale-type Theorem for Strict Contactomorphisms of Sasakian Spheres
item.description: arXiv:2312.15996v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Legendrian mean curvature flow in $\eta$-Einstein Sasakian manifolds by parabolic rescalings which preserve the contact structure. In a compact $\eta$-Einstein Sasakian manifold, regular or not, the contact tangent flows at a Type I singularity are, up to vertical translations of their components, self-similar flows of Legendrian self-shrinkers in the Heisenberg group, and they are unions of Legendrian planes. When the Reeb orbits are not closed, as on the irregular Sasaki--Einstein manifolds, the leaf space of the Reeb foliation is not a K\"ahler manifold or orbifold, and this result does not follow by projecting the flow to a Lagrangian mean curvature flow; its proof combines local transverse estimates with a Gaussian density localised in a flow box of the Reeb foliation. In a regular manifold a Type I singularity can only form at a point of transverse Gaussian density at least $2$. We apply the analysis to strict contactomorphisms $\varphi$ of the standard Sasakian sphere $\mathbb S^{2k+1}$, whose Legendrian graphs lie in the $\eta$-Einstein manifold $(\mathbb S^{2k+1}\times\mathbb S^{2k+1})/\mathbb S^1$. The Jacobian of a Legendrian graph obeys a reaction--diffusion equation whose quadratic term is a sum of squares when $k=1$ and is indefinite when $k\geq2$. For every strict contactomorphism of $\mathbb S^3$, and for every pinched strict contactomorphism of $\mathbb S^{2k+1}$, $k\geq2$, the contact blow-ups of the flow of its Legendrian graph are flat, the flow exists for all time and, up to a rotation along the Reeb flow, converges exponentially to the graph of an element of $U(k+1)$. In particular such a $\varphi$ is isotopic to $U(k+1)$ through strict contactomorphisms.
item.dc:creator: Shu-Cheng Chang, Chin-Tung Wu, Liuyang Zhang

item.title: Uniqueness of Ricci flow with scaling invariant estimates
item.description: arXiv:2503.20292v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we prove uniqueness for complete non-compact Ricci flow with scaling invariant curvature bound. This generalizes the earlier work of Chen-Zhu, Kotschwar and covers most of the example of Ricci flows with unbounded curvature. In dimension three, we use it to show that complete Ricci flow starting from uniformly non-collapsed, non-negatively curved manifold is unique, extending the strong uniqueness Theorem of Chen. This is based on solving Ricci-harmonic map heat flow in unbounded curvature background.
item.dc:creator: Man-Chun Lee

item.title: Non-compact Ricci Solitons of Finite Volume with Potential Field of Constant Length
item.description: arXiv:2607.22394v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study non-compact Ricci solitons of finite volume whose potential vector field has constant length. Under the assumptions that the scalar curvature is constant along the integral curves of the potential field and that a natural divergence term is integrable on the unit tangent bundle, we prove that such Ricci solitons are necessarily trivial. As applications, we characterise $3$-dimensional Ricci solitons of constant length and of finite volume on almost $\alpha$-cosymplectic manifolds. In fact, we show that these spaces are indeed compact quotients of Euclidean spaces. We also study complete, non-compact and finite volume contact metric manifolds in dimension $3$ admitting a Reeb vector field as a Ricci soliton. We show that it is a compact spherical space form. We include some examples to illustrate the necessity of the finite-volume and constant-length assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Hemangi Madhusudan Shah, Sharief Deshmukh, Mohammad Aqib

item.title: Eventual Monotonicity of the Willmore Energy under Mean Curvature Flow
item.description: arXiv:2609.18378v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish the eventual monotonicity of the Willmore deficit \( \int_{\Sigma}H^2\,d\mu-16\pi \) along the mean curvature flow of smooth closed embedded strictly convex surfaces in \( \mathbb R^3 \), thereby complementing Huisken's exponential convergence with an eventual monotonicity property. As a consequence, the Hawking mass is eventually nondecreasing along the contracting mean curvature flow, in contrast with the usual inclusion monotonicity expected of the Hawking mass. We also discuss totally umbilical solutions in three-dimensional space forms, where the monotonicity directions of the Willmore energy and the Hawking mass depend on the sign of the ambient sectional curvature.
item.dc:creator: Yuyue Chen, Shiying Wu

item.title: Complete Self-Shrinkers in Arbitrary Codimension with Positive Constant Scalar Curvature and $S\le 1$
item.description: arXiv:2609.19464v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let \(X:M^n\to\mathbb R^{n+p}\) be an \(n\)-dimensional complete self-shrinker in arbitrary codimension \(p\ge 1\). Suppose that the scalar curvature \(R\) is a positive constant and that the squared norm \(S\) of the second fundamental form satisfies \(S\le 1\). We prove that \(S\equiv 1\) and that \(X\) is isometric to either the round sphere \(S^n(\sqrt n)\) or the standard generalized cylinder \(S^k(\sqrt k)\times\mathbb R^{n-k}\), \(2\le k\le n-1\). In particular, no new higher-codimension examples occur under these assumptions. The proof uses an algebraic lemma which yields a uniform positive lower bound for the Bakry--\'Emery Ricci curvature, together with the comparison theorem of Wei--Wylie, the equivalence of finite Gaussian volume and polynomial volume growth due to Cheng--Zhou, and the gap theorem of Cao--Li.
item.dc:creator: Shunzi Guo

item.title: On Lorentzian Lie groups of Nonzero Constant Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2609.40017v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate Lie groups endowed with left-invariant Lorentzian metrics of nonzero constant sectional curvature. We first revisit Heintze's theory and obtain a characterization of the Lie algebras of Riemannian Lie groups of negative constant curvature. We also extend classical results of Nomizu and Barnet to the pseudo-Riemannian setting by constructing a large family of Lie groups carrying incomplete left-invariant metrics of constant sectional curvature. We then describe Lorentzian Lie algebras of nonzero constant curvature according to the causal nature of their center and derived ideal. This description is complete except when the derived ideal is Lorentzian, for which we obtain a complete classification in dimension four. We show that every left-invariant Lorentzian metric of nonzero constant curvature on \(\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb R)\) is bi-invariant and complete. Moreover, a semisimple Lie group admits a complete left-invariant Lorentzian metric of nonzero constant curvature if and only if it is locally isomorphic to \(\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb R)\). We also characterize \(\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb R)\) through the existence of a noncentral spacelike left-invariant Killing vector field. Finally, we classify Lorentzian Lie algebras of nonzero constant curvature in dimensions at most four.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Boucetta

item.title: The interpolation method for the complex Hessian equation on compact K\"ahler manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.07852v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In current work, we delve into the study of complex Hessian equations on compact K\"ahler manifolds. By imposing a constraint on both the bisectional curvature and the oscillation of the solution, we demonstrate that the Laplacian estimate can be linearly controlled by its gradient estimate. Consequently, we are able to derive gradient estimate for the solution using a standard interpolation argument, without the need to employ the blow-up technique. As an application, we demonstrate that when the right-hand side of the complex Hessian equations approximate 1 in the $L^1$ norm, the desired gradient estimate is obtained.
item.dc:creator: Jiaogen Zhang, Xi Zhang

item.title: Explicit Ricci-flat Metrics on Kummer K3 Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.11077v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a convergent explicit representation of the Ricci-flat K\"ahler metrics supplied by the Calabi--Yau theorem in a one-parameter family of classes on a fixed Kummer K3 surface. An explicit radial background has normalized Monge--Amp\`ere residual \(O(a^4)\). Its scalar Green operator \(G_a\) is represented by periodic Ewald kernels, separated radial kernels, finite-dimensional Schur complements, and convergent Neumann series. The coefficients are defined by \(U_{a,1}=-G_af_a\) and \(U_{a,n}=G_a\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}Q_a(U_{a,j},U_{a,n-j})\), where \(Q_a\) is the polarized quadratic Monge--Amp\`ere term. A Green estimate of order \(a^{-1}\) gives a first correction of order \(a^3\) and a convergence parameter of order \(a^2\). A Catalan majorant proves absolute convergence on the entire smooth surface for every sufficiently small fixed \(a\). The sum defines a positive form solving the volume equation; comparison identifies the sum with the smooth normalized Calabi--Yau potential. We also record sufficient analytic conditions for the same recursion on collapsing elliptic K3 surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Jixiang Fu, Yunyang Xiao, Shing-Tung Yau

item.title: A semi-discrete scheme for horizontal mean curvature flow in the Heisenberg group
item.description: arXiv:2610.20054v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The horizontal mean curvature flow is a geometric evolution associated with the horizontal perimeter in sub-Riemannian spaces. In this paper, we introduce a minimizing movement scheme for this flow in the first Heisenberg group $\mathbb{H}$, and prove the existence of a flat flow which is locally $1/2$-H\"older continuous in time, with respect to the $L^1$-distance. The construction applies to arbitrary bounded sets of finite horizontal perimeter and does not require smoothness or symmetry of the initial datum.
item.dc:creator: A. Cesaroni, M. Novaga, P. Pozzi

item.title: Second Maximum of a Gaussian Random Field and Exact (t-)Spacing test
item.description: arXiv:2406.18397v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this article, we introduce the novel concept of the second maximum of a Gaussian random field defined on a Riemannian manifold: Once the field reaches its global maximum at a point $t_1$, the second maximum is the largest value of the field away from $t_1$, after the value and the gradient of the field at $t_1$ have been removed. This statistic serves as a powerful tool for characterizing the distribution of the global maximum. By employing an ad-hoc Kac-Rice formula, we derive the explicit distribution of the maximum, conditioned on the second maximum and the independent part of the Riemannian Hessian (the part of the Hessian at $t_1$ that is independent of the value and the gradient of the field at $t_1$). This approach yields an exact test based on the spacing between these maxima, which we refer to as the spacing test. We investigate the applicability of this test for detecting sparse alternatives in Gaussian symmetric tensors, continuous sparse deconvolution, and two-layered neural networks with smooth rectifiers. Theoretical results are supported by numerical experiments that illustrate the calibration and power of the proposed procedures. More generally, we provide a framework for applying the spacing test to continuous sparse regression for any Gaussian random field on a Riemannian manifold. Furthermore, when the variance-covariance function is known only up to a scaling factor, we derive an exact Studentized version of the procedure, coined the t-spacing test. We show that this test is perfectly calibrated under the null hypothesis and exhibits high power for detecting sparse alternatives. As a corollary, we derive an exact, non-asymptotic test for the spiked tensor model without requiring prior knowledge of the noise level.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Marc Aza\"is, Federico Dalmao, Yohann De Castro

item.title: Stability of the catenoid for the hyperbolic vanishing mean curvature equation in 4 spatial dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2411.08366v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish the asymptotic stability of the catenoid, as a nonflat stationary solution to the hyperbolic vanishing mean curvature (HVMC) equation in Minkowski space $\mathbb{R}^{1 + (n + 1)}$ for $n = 4$. Our main result is under a ``codimension-$1$'' assumption on initial perturbation, modulo suitable translation and boost (i.e. modulation), without any symmetry assumptions. In comparison to the $n \geq 5$ case addressed by L\"{u}hrmann-Oh-Shahshahani arxiv:2212.05620, proving catenoid stability in $4$ dimensions shares additional difficulties with its $3$ dimensional analog, namely the slower spatial decay of the catenoid and slower temporal decay of waves. To overcome these difficulties in the $n = 3$ case, the strong Huygens principle, as well as a miraculous cancellation in the source term, plays an important role in arxiv:2409.05968 to obtain strong late time tails. In $n = 4$ dimensions, without these special structural advantages, our novelty is to introduce an appropriate commutator vector field to derive a new hierarchy of estimates with higher $r^p$-weights so that an improved pointwise decay can be established. We expect this to be applicable for proving improved late time tails of other quasilinear wave equations in even dimensions or wave equations with inverse square potential.
item.dc:creator: Ning Tang

item.title: Large-scale rank and geometry of the Lipschitz metric on geodesic currents
item.description: arXiv:2610.03359v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a closed orientable surface of genus at least 2, we study the large-scale geometry of the (symmetrized) Lipschitz metric on its space of projective filling geodesic currents. We show that the rank and, hence, asymptotic dimension of the space of filling geodesic currents is infinite. This gives the first example of a natural proper space associated to a closed surface, with a metrically proper isometric action of the mapping class group, that has infinite asymptotic dimension. In contrast, we show that any finite simplex of geodesic currents has rank uniformly bounded above by $8g-9$. We then show a sufficient criterion for its rank and asymptotic dimension to be equal to $8g-9$ and construct examples satisfying it, thus showing the bound is sharp. We further prove that Teichm\"uller space equipped with the Lipschitz metric has rank equal to $3g-3$. In particular, the space of projective filling geodesic currents and the Teichm\"uller space are not quasi-isometric.
item.dc:creator: D\'idac Mart\'inez-Granado, Jenya Sapir

item.title: Stability for a formally determined Lorentzian inverse problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.10413v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the inverse problem of recovering a potential $q$, depending on space and time, in the wave equation $(\Box_g+q)u=0$ on a Lorentzian manifold. We prove Lipschitz stability for a formally determined version of this problem under a \textit{null-cone foliation} assumption. As a consequence, we obtain uniqueness in the Lorentzian Calder\'on problem for $q$ under this assumption. Our approach is based on a modification of the Bukhgeim--Klibanov method using distorted plane waves.
item.dc:creator: Spyridon Filippas, Lauri Oksanen
